newsitem.title: USA: Search warrants issued on Columbia/HCA sites.
newsitem.headline: Search warrants issued on Columbia/HCA sites.

text.p: Hospital giant Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp. said Wednesday that locations in five states were served with federal search warrants.
Columbia/HCA said in a statement that it believes the warrants "requested various records and documents primarily in two separate areas: hospital laboratory billing and home care operations."
The company said locations in Florida, Tennessee, Texas, North Carolina and Utah were served with the warrants. The company's stock tumbled
$4.94 to $34 on the New York Stock Exchange following the report. Columbia was the second most active issue, with volume of over 11.6 million shares.
Chairman Richard Scott, speaking at the Montgomery Securities Healthcare Conference in New York, said he did not know the exact nature of the raids or what the FBI might be seeking.
However, he indicated that he suspected the investigation might concern "blood kits through emergency rooms."
He added, "I don't know if this is what this is."

It was not immediately clear if the search warrants served Wednesday were related to search warrants served in March at Columbia/HCA's El Paso, Texas, operations, or to subsequent news reports about federal probes into other operations.
When asked if any company executives had been subpoenaed, Scott said, "I can't answer these questions."
